clue.text: Dish for one, two officers race to eat first

indicators.note: two officers means the same abbreviation is written twice over

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word eat is used

explanation.surface: A pair of officers dash off to get their meal before anyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocotte is a small ovenproof pot in which a single portion is cooked and served.

clue.text: Old novelist may, in England, end life

parts.note: in Britain, may is the everyday name for the hawthorn tree and its blossom

indicators.note: end means only the closing letter of the word life is taken

explanation.surface: A veteran writer might, in England, decide to bring their days to a close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' looks like a verb, but it is the blossoming tree British people call may.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne was a nineteenth-century American author of The Scarlet Letter.

clue.text: I'm also mistaken for an East African

indicators.note: mistaken suggests the letters have been got wrong and must be put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that people often take them for a person from East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Somalia, a country in the Horn of Africa, is called this.

clue.text: Odd! MOT garage excluding a warranty

indicators.note: odd describes something strange, signalling that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars, done at a garage

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised that a vehicle-testing workshop offers no guarantee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excluding' tells you to take an A out: MOT GARAGE without one A leaves MOTGARGE, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortgage is a legal pledge of property as security for a loan, a kind of guarantee.

clue.text: Appearance of optimism, initially, at a ministerial reshuffle

indicators.note: a reshuffle reorganises positions, so these letters are put in a new order
initially means just the opening letter of the word optimism is taken

explanation.surface: A government reorganisation of ministers brings a sudden show of hope.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is O (from 'optimism, initially') with AT, A and MINISTERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A materialisation is the coming into view or taking shape of something, an apparition.

clue.text: It's not often you come across this half-cooked piece of fish at top dinner

definitions.text: It's not often you come across this

parts.note: rare meat is only lightly cooked, so half-cooked means rare
a fin is a part of a fish

indicators.note: top means the first letter of the word dinner is used

explanation.surface: A diner is offered undercooked fish as the highlight of a fancy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something seldom encountered and valuable is called a lucky discovery of this kind.

clue.text: Figure legendary for pithy remark

definitions.meaning: a little bearded creature of folklore, often seen as a garden statue
a short wise saying, a maxim or aphorism

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a folklore goblin guarding underground treasure and an aphorism, from Greek gnome, opinion.

clue.text: Greet us, for a change, by this means?

definitions.text: Greet us, for a change, by this means?

indicators.note: for a change says the letters of the words greet us are altered into another order

explanation.surface: Someone suggests greeting people differently, by a wave or nod perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave or nod is a movement of the body used to convey a meaning such as hello.

clue.text: Vessel one gets to cook this vegetable

definitions.text: Vessel one gets to cook this vegetable

parts.note: a pot is a cooking vessel
a means one, as in a single item
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook takes a saucepan to boil a spud.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: the vegetable you put in a vessel to cook.
explanation.definitionFit: A spud is a starchy tuber boiled in a pan, exactly what the cook puts in the vessel.

clue.text: Slow mover tries too strenuously

indicators.note: strenuously suggests vigorous working over of the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A sluggish person makes far too much effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The shelled reptile is proverbially slow, as in the fable of the hare.

clue.text: Funny, a car to be used in this contest!

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, telling us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: It would be amusing to drive a car in this competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual rowing contest on the Thames between Oxford and Cambridge universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing competition between two crews is a race of this kind.

clue.text: Worry pointless over misshapen toe — it's not fully developed

indicators.note: over is read as covering, so one piece goes round the other
pointless means dropping a compass point, here the letter for south

parts.note: to fuss is to worry

indicators.note: misshapen means the letters of toe are bent into another order

explanation.surface: Someone frets needlessly about a deformed toe that has not grown properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' means losing a compass point, here S for south; 'over' is read as going round, so the shortened worry encloses the reshaped toe.
explanation.definitionFit: An unborn baby in the womb is still growing and so not yet complete.

clue.text: Street broil -I hurled cones

indicators.note: hurled means thrown about, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: the letter I is printed with a dash before it

explanation.surface: Someone in the road, overheated, flings pine cones.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobili are the cone-shaped fruiting bodies of pines and similar plants.

clue.text: Made invalid Anne dull — just shuffling around

indicators.note: shuffling around means the letters of Anne dull are mixed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Anne, a boring person, merely shifts her feet about.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel a contract or marriage is to declare it void, without legal force.

clue.text: Silver underwear?

parts.note: the pirate captain of Treasure Island lends his first names to warm full-length undergarments worn in winter

explanation.definitionFit: These are warm full-length underpants, sharing their name with the pirate Silver's first names.

clue.text: Gives ref a boot — but it seems he needs two

indicators.note: gives means bends or yields, so the letters of ref a boot shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A footballer kicks the referee, who apparently has no shoes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a player who 'gives the ref a boot'; but someone bare-footed needs two boots, a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shoeless would need a pair of boots, so the joke is that they lack both.

clue.text: Learned folk with sex appeal are rejected — first to be fired

indicators.note: first tells us this piece goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: something fired, as a fire or lamp, is lit

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the run made by these two words is read backwards

parts.note: IT is the old slang for sex appeal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Intellectuals who are attractive are turned down, and the first to go loses their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses ITARE to give ERATI, which follows LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Literati are educated people interested in literature, the intelligentsia.

clue.text: Roman goddess follows in state

indicators.note: follows means the goddess comes after the other piece in the answer

parts.note: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt

explanation.surface: A deity of ancient Rome comes next in a sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is a Midwestern US state, capital Indianapolis.

clue.text: Is ashen, upset by sacking

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of is ashen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone turns pale, distressed at being dismissed from work.
explanation.definitionFit: Hessian is a coarse jute cloth used for sacks.

clue.text: Used runners when travelling and was murdered, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is identified by its sound when spoken

parts.note: slayed is a past form of slay, to kill

explanation.surface: Someone travelled on skis or runners and met a violent end, by report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' are the blades of a sledge, not people running.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling by sledge over snow on its runners is to go by a horse-drawn sledge.

clue.text: Run out and die

definitions.meaning: to come to an end, as a passport or lease does

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to lapse when a term ends and to pass away.

clue.text: Can be ingested though strangely belied

indicators.note: strangely means oddly arranged, asking us to reorder the letters of belied

explanation.surface: Something can be swallowed, even though its look gives a false impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is fit to eat can safely be swallowed.

clue.text: Bad start for inexperienced student taking part in it?

definitions.text: Bad start for inexperienced student taking part in it?

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of the word bad is taken

parts.note: raw means green, untrained
L is the learner plate sign, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A green learner gets off to a poor beginning by joining a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a punch-up is a bad start for a novice who joins it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fight is a rough, noisy scuffle, a poor beginning for any newcomer involved.

clue.text: Water control — hard on river — formerly was a bar.

parts.note: a tap controls the flow of water
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A water valve beside a river used to serve as a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formerly was' is linking, hinting the term is old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A taphouse is an old name for an inn or tavern where beer was drawn from the barrel.

clue.text: Acorn I am stirring into this dish

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters of acorn I am are rearranged

explanation.surface: An acorn says it is being mixed into a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a pasta served as a dish, often baked with cheese.

clue.text: Riotous behaviour breaks into grand anarchy

indicators.note: breaks into means the answer is found inside the run of grand anarchy

explanation.surface: A riot erupts amid widespread lawlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: Randan is a dated word for a spree or uproarious carousing.

clue.text: Stiffening, seeing the French in Scots' attire

indicators.note: in signals that one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tartan is the checked woollen cloth worn by Scots
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: French visitors are seen wearing Scottish kilts that look stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarlatan is a thin open muslin, heavily starched, used as a stiffening fabric.
